ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a circuit in which an AC source supplies two parallel branches. At the top node, the source current I_s enters the node along the upper wire and then splits; the middle branch is R and L in series, with branch current I_RL downward; the right branch is capacitor C, and the capacitor current I_C is also downward according to the direction shown in the figure. The figure gives V_s = 1∠0 V and marks I_RL = √2∠(-π/4) A. Then reason: According to the method in the problem statement, apply KCL at the top node, and with the current directions consistent with the arrows in the figure, I_C = I_s - I_RL. Convert the R-L branch current to rectangular coordinates: I_RL = √2∠(-π/4) = √2(cos(-π/4) + j sin(-π/4)) = 1 - j A. The source current phasor is I_s = 1 + j A. Therefore I_C = (1 + j) - (1 - j) = 2j A.

Then I_C = (1 + j) - (1 - j) = +j2 A.
